question: Should upgrades automatically discard only unversioned failed attachment queue records carrying the historical stack-overflow signature while retaining marked current failures?
rationale: The branch intentionally deletes persisted user queue state to prevent replay of records created by the old bug; tests establish the narrow mechanism, but accepting that data-retention boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve targeted cleanup
options.body: Accept the private version marker and drop only matching unversioned legacy attachment failures after exact-head proof confirms the surrounding send flow.

options.title: Land parser fixes only
options.body: Remove the persisted-queue cleanup and preserve every failed record, leaving stale-record recovery for a separate explicit product path.

options.title: Split cleanup for follow-up
options.body: Merge stack-safe parsing separately and keep the state migration in a focused follow-up with dedicated upgrade and recovery proof.

recommendation.title: Approve targeted cleanup
recommendation.body: Accept the private version marker and drop only matching unversioned legacy attachment failures after exact-head proof confirms the surrounding send flow.

likelyOwner.reason: They co-authored and merged the adjacent current-main attachment stack-safety work and are the strongest history-backed owner for deciding compatibility with that pipeline.
